slides.title: ADHD cleaning myths I believed for 30 years
slides.sub: Myth 3 kept me stuck the longest

slides.title: Myth: I need to be motivated first
slides.body: Truth: motivation usually shows up after we start. Start with 2 minutes. Momentum does the rest.

slides.title: Myth: clean the whole room or it doesn't count
slides.body: Truth: one cleared surface counts. Our brains need wins we can see, not all-or-nothing.

slides.title: Myth: I need the perfect system first
slides.body: Truth: researching systems feels productive but moves zero dishes. A messy system you use beats a perfect one you don't.

slides.title: Myth: tidy people have more discipline
slides.body: Truth: many of them have brains that remember things in cabinets. We need things visible and close.

slides.title: Myth: if I fall off the routine, I failed
slides.body: Truth: every routine breaks. What matters is how fast you restart. Plan the restart, not a perfect streak.

slides.title: I'm not bad at cleaning. I was using instructions written for a different brain.
Instructions for OUR brain
slides.body: The Messy Brain Home Reset is the 7-day system built for ADHD brains. No shame, no perfection. Link in bio.
